text: Qinhuangdao Shanhaiguan Airport (IATA: SHP, ICAO: ZBSH) is a military airport located in the Shanhaiguan District of Qinhuangdao, Hebei Province, China, situated 15 kilometres (9.3 mi) from the city center. From 1985 to 2016, it also functioned as the civilian airport for Qinhuangdao. On 31 March 2016, the newly constructed Qinhuangdao Beidaihe Airport began operations, and all civil flights were transferred to it, causing Shanhaiguan Airport to revert to sole military use, although there are plans for general aviation. On 13 September 1971, Marshall Lin Biao, China's Vice Premier and Minister of Defense, attempted to flee China from Shanhaiguan Airport in a Hawker Siddeley Trident, allegedly after a failed coup; the plane crashed in Mongolia, killing all nine people on board, including Lin Biao, his wife Ye Qun, and their son Lin Liguo. The airport opened to civil flights on 15 April 1985 and operated flights to over 20 Chinese cities. Between 2007 and a later period, it temporarily operated international flights to Yakutsk and Blagoveshchensk in Russia. Throughout its thirty-year operation, it maintained a perfect safety record. Although expanded in preparation for the 2008 Beijing Olympics, its military status limited further development. A new airport, Qinhuangdao Beidaihe Airport, was proposed in 2004 and received State Council approval in July 2009; construction began in April 2012 and was completed in 2016. In its final full year of operation in 2015, Shanhaiguan Airport served 156,000 passengers. The airport features a single runway measuring 2,500 metres (8,200 ft) (class 4C), capable of handling mid-sized passenger jets such as the Boeing 737 and the Airbus A320, with six aircraft parking aprons and 200 car parking spaces.
